Subset a dicom_volume While Preserving World Geometry

Source: R/dicom-volume.R
sub-.dicom_volume.Rd

Extracts a sub-volume from a 3D or 4D dicom_volume, automatically shifting the physical origin affine[1:3, 4] to the world coordinate of the new first voxel, scaling/flipping affine columns and direction / spacing for strided or reversed index sequences, slicing frame_meta, and flagging irregular spacing if non-uniform indices are supplied.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'dicom_volume'
x[..., drop = FALSE]

Arguments

x

A dicom_volume object.

...

Row, column, slice (and optional 4th-dimension frame) subscripts.

drop

Logical. Defaults to FALSE, preserving the "dicom_volume" container and 4x4 affine even when subsetting selects a single slice (vol[, , 2]) or crops a single-slice 2D modality (dx_vol[2:8, 3:10, ]). If TRUE and subsetting reduces any spatial dimension to length 1, returns the dropped base R matrix or vector; when subsetting a single temporal frame from a 4D volume (vol[, , , 2, drop = TRUE]) with all 3 spatial dimensions > 1, drops the 4th dimension and returns a 3D dicom_volume.

Value

A dicom_volume object (always when drop = FALSE, or when 3-4 spatial/temporal dimensions remain under drop = TRUE), or a base R array/matrix/vector when drop = TRUE reduces spatial dimensions < 3.

Examples

vox <- array(seq_len(10 * 12 * 6), dim = c(10L, 12L, 6L))
aff <- diag(c(0.5, 0.5, 2.0, 1.0))
vol <- new_dicom_volume(vox, affine = aff, modality = "CT")
sub <- vol[2:8, 3:10, 2:5]
dim(sub)
#> [1] 7 8 4
single <- vol[, , 2]
dim(single)
#> [1] 10 12  1
